title: Standardize SDK connection patterns and enterprise triage across languages
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem statement: Enterprise customers repeatedly request language-specific SDK behaviors for connection setup (auth handshakes, token refresh, resumable streaming) that vary widely between languages. This creates maintenance overhead, leads to inconsistent security posture, and slows onboarding for high-value customers. Goal: produce a small, prescriptive set of 'connection patterns' (session-init, token-rotation, streaming-handshake, reconnect/backoff) and an associated prioritization matrix that maps customer signals (deployment mode, security requirements, expected qps, streaming usage) to SDK work items by language. Scope: triage framework + RFC + prioritized backlog of 6 candidate SDK tasks (examples below). Out of scope: full implementation for all languages in this ticket — this ticket will deliver the decision framework, per-language gap analysis, and prioritized implementation plan for next cycle.
acceptance_criteria: 1) RFC published in Confluence with diagrams and examples for each connection pattern. 2) Per-language gap table completed for top 6 supported languages (Python, Node, Java, Go, Ruby, C#). 3) Prioritized backlog (epics or Linear tickets) created and linked for execution. 4) Stakeholder sign-off from Security, SDK leads, and Solutions Engineering. 5) Initial design for server-side compatibility tests and a minimal reference implementation for Python streaming handshake.
success_metrics: - Time-to-onboard enterprise customers for SDK-based streaming reduced from 6 weeks to 3 weeks (target). - Number of bespoke enterprise SDK patches decreases by 50% within two quarters. - Reduction in security-related SDK support tickets by 40%.
proposed_connection_patterns: - Session-init: single RPC to exchange metadata (client_id, environment, requested scopes) and return connection token + capabilities. - Token-rotation: short, well-documented interface for silent refresh with example interceptors/middleware per language. - Streaming-handshake: explicit start/ack pattern allowing client to opt into resumable IDs and server-assigned cursor tokens. - Resumable-reconnect: deterministic reconnection semantics (cursor + seq) and idempotency hints. - Graceful-fallback: client-level policy to fall back to polling or smaller chunked streaming when server signals degraded capacity.
candidate_work_items: 1) Python: streaming-handshake reference + interceptor (est 3). 2) Node: standard token-rotation middleware + README (est 2). 3) Java: session-init builder API + integration test (est 5). 4) Go: reconnect/backoff strategy in client lib (est 3). 5) Ruby: simplified sync wrapper with explicit token refresh hooks (est 2). 6) C#: sample for resumable streams + docs (est 3).
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Broad compatibility vs idiomatic language APIs: aim for small consistent surface but allow thin language-specific wrappers. - Operational complexity: adding resumable streaming semantics requires server-side support and test harnesses. - Security review needed for token lifecycle changes; delaying review risks rework. - Prioritization risk: focusing on languages with fewer current customers may delay revenue-impacting work for top customers.
stakeholder_feedback_summary: - Security: insists on KMS-backed token generation, short TTLs, and explicit audit events in Console. - Solutions Eng: wants clear examples for SaaS and Dedicated flows (token exchange via customer proxy). - SDK Leads: prefer minimal core interface + composer wrappers to keep maintenance low. - Sales/CS: prioritize Python and Node, then Java/Go for large enterprise on-ramp.
proposed_prioritization_matrix: Axes: customer_signal (High/Medium/Low for enterprise spend) x technical_complexity (Low/Medium/High). Mapping: High enterprise + Low complexity -> P0; High enterprise + Medium complexity -> P1; Medium enterprise + Low complexity -> P1; Low enterprise + High complexity -> P3. Streaming-heavy customers with Dedicated/Private deployments get elevated priority due to data-path constraints.
